findings.statement: PMID:42473996 reports CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low background expression in normal kidney tissue, and CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC, 'warranting prospective validation' (early-stage evidence). High CA9 PET uptake is associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function alterations. PMID:35795483 also reports CAIX mRNA increased in HIV-associated kidney cancer. Omics (rank 1) and drugs (girentuximab) agree. The data-only profiles show no prognostic signal for CA9, so the literature supports it as a diagnostic/imaging target rather than a prognostic marker.
PMID:34970493 (mouse TRACK model) reports that mitochondrial Ndufa4l2 enhances lipid deposition and Ca9 expression in early ccRCC, linking COXFA4L2 upstream of CA9.

PMID:38195301 states CD70 is commonly overexpressed in renal cell carcinoma and minimally expressed in normal human tissue, making it a potential therapeutic target for advanced RCC; CD70 correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins in ccRCC. PMID:39510586 reports high, specific ccRCC expression as a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target, associates expression with overall survival and metastasis, and describes 68Ga-labelled CD70-specific single-domain antibodies (RCCB3, RCCB6) as radiotracers. Preclinical/early translational; the data-only profile also supports tumour-up expression.

PMID:40852386 reports ALDOB is a prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target in ccRCC, with IHC showing it notably diminished in tumour relative to adjacent normal tissue, and linked to infiltrating Treg, Th17 cells and neutrophils. PMID:38655323 concludes ALDOB may be an independent prognostic predictor in KIRC with reference value for immunotherapy; PMID:37083815 is pan-cancer bioinformatics. Evidence is mostly bioinformatic plus one IHC cohort; the data biomarker profile is high but the target profile is low, so the 'target' wording is speculative (loss of expression is not directly druggable).

PMID:41399267 reports NNMT significantly upregulated in ccRCC tumours, high NNMT correlating with worse overall and disease-specific survival (P < 0.001), and calls it a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target with transcriptomic, clinical and functional validation. PMID:37523719 describes potent NNMT inhibitors (II559, II802) with over 5000-fold selectivity versus related methyltransferases, a chemistry-level (not ccRCC clinical) tractability signal. Literature and the data-only profiles (target and biomarker) agree.

PMID:37760940 concludes ENO2 is a potential diagnostic biomarker that independently predicts ccRCC prognosis and promotes progression through glycolysis (Warburg effect). PMID:39091581 shows ENO2 high in ccRCC cell lines and that its knockdown inhibits glycolysis, promotes ferroptosis and affects mitochondrial function. PMID:36313709 links ENO2 to overall survival and PMID:34467977 reports serum NSE as an independent risk factor for intraocular metastasis in RCC. Mostly single-lab in vitro and bioinformatic studies; no drug evidence.

PMID:35120484 (bioinformatic) reports FCER1G abundantly expressed in ccRCC tumours, positively related to macrophage infiltration and T cell suppression, prognostic in patients treated with nivolumab but not everolimus, and that combining FCER1G with CD68 may be a promising postoperative prognostic index. The expression likely reflects immune infiltration (the data show a strong negative purity correlation), so it is a stromal/immune marker rather than a tumour-intrinsic target.

Contradictory literature on direction: PMID:36204178 reports MT1G downregulated in ccRCC versus normal renal tissue, a negative ferroptosis regulator and poor-prognosis biomarker; PMID:38906969 observes low MT1G in tumour tissue yet high expression correlating with advanced stage and poorer prognosis, and shows elevated MT1G promotes growth and metastasis, inhibiting CPT1B via H3K14 trimethylation to enhance lipid droplets. PMID:40247376 finds SAP30 inhibits MT1G transcription, impairing zinc delivery to p53. Tumour-down in the omics, but pro-tumour in functional work: unresolved.

PMID:41158242 (pan-cancer) reports ABAT significantly underexpressed in KIRC among other cancers and predicting poor prognosis in KIRC; PMID:41813748 shows ABAT overexpression suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, acting via cGAS-STING and interaction with PRMT5 to enhance interferon signaling. Supportive but mostly non-ccRCC-specific or pan-cancer; a vigabatrin drug link exists in the ranking but no ccRCC treatment data in the corpus.

PMID:36123895 reports SLC22A8 protein, phosphoprotein and DNA methylation levels lower in ccRCC than normal tissue, low methylation predicting poor overall survival, and that SLC22A8 can be used as a prognostic biomarker with links to immune infiltration. Single bioinformatic study; consistent with strong data-only biomarker profile.

PMID:42028950 reports SLC16A3-mediated lactate export activates macrophage ERK signaling in a GPR81-dependent manner, promotes M2 macrophage polarization and suppresses CD8+ T-cell function, driving immune evasion in ccRCC through an autocrine GPR81-ERK-c-MYC loop. A single recent mechanistic paper; consistent with tumour-up expression in the data.

UMOD is reported downregulated in ccRCC in several studies: PMID:36899967 (hypo-down methylation/expression cluster), PMID:37275334 (validation of a bioinformatic signature) and PMID:35795483 (HIV-associated kidney cancer, by PCR). These are descriptive down-regulation reports with no prognostic or therapeutic claim, so UMOD is best seen as a loss-of-normal-tubule marker.

caveats: SCARB1 and PIGR rank 5 and 6 with strong omics and Open Targets genetic support but have zero literature relations in this corpus; a search for SCARB1 returned only unrelated RCC abstracts. They are data-supported candidates without literature backing.
FABP1 and NPHS2 (ranks 9-10) have only 2 literature relations each and were not reviewed in detail.

Most literature is single-study, bioinformatic (TCGA-derived) signatures; only CA9 (PET proof-of-concept) and CD70 (radiotracers) have translational evidence, and both authors call for prospective validation.

Many top-ranked genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, ABAT, MT1G) are downregulated in tumour; these are biomarkers, not directly druggable targets, so 'target' claims for them are not supported by the data-only target profile.
MT1G literature is contradictory (low in tumour yet high expression linked to poor prognosis and tumour promotion).
The ranking was read only to the top 15 because the full output was too large; genes beyond rank 15 were not reviewed.
